route: published subscale/total mean + SD (route 3); per-item ordering via GRM discrimination trend and monotone per-item means (routes 1 and 8)
evidence: Route 3 (published totals) + route 1/8 (per-item ordering), against Zanesco et al. (2024) BRM 56:7707-7727. (a) OPTION-TO-RESP DIRECTION: live table restricted to the source file's own Exclude==0 flag gives N=355, participant mean-of-means 2.508, SD 0.880 -- identical at 3 dp to the published Table 1 value for Goller et al. (2020), 2.508 (0.880), N=355; the full live table is 366 participants, 2.539 (0.906). A reversed anchor order would require 6-2.508 = 3.492, which is 1.0 scale points away, so resp 1 = 'Completely on-task' and resp 5 = 'Completely off-task' as shipped. (b) ITEM-CODE ORDERING: fitting the 2P graded response model to the same 355 x 36 live matrix gives discrimination values 0.84-2.87 (published 0.84-2.54) and a quadratic trend of a_i over probe index of R2=0.839, F(2,33)=86.08 -- matching the published R2=0.839, F(2,33)=86.08 exactly; 0 of 2000 random item-to-occasion permutations reach R2>=0.839. Per-item mean rating rises monotonically 1.6 (T1) to 3.0 (T36), Spearman with probe index 0.984, i.e. off-task ratings increase with time on task. So T1..T36 are the 36 probes in administered order, and data/Zanesco_2023.py takes those codes straight from the deposit's headers. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: the literal on-screen stem, which no source publishes and which is therefore blank in the shipped file; and the three interior anchors 2, 3 and 4 individually -- they are transcribed with the source's own explicit numbering, but a mean pins only the direction of the scale, not each intermediate label, and the ordering route is a global trend rather than a test of any adjacent pair. Hence PARTIAL, not VERIFIED.
